Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Features | Opinion Daily Insight for CEOs: The CEO’s Role in Driving Year-End Performance 2 November 2026 11:26pm Audio By Carbonatix
November marks a critical stage in the organisation’s performance journey. With only two months remaining in 2026, CEOs must intensify their focus on delivering strategic commitments, closing performance gaps, and ensuring that resources are directed towards the results that matter most.
Year-end performance does not improve through pressure alone. It requires clear priorities, timely decisions, executive ownership, and consistent monitoring of progress.
The CEO must create the urgency and discipline needed to move the organization from intention to measurable results.
✅ Convene the executive team to review the organization’s year-end performance position.
✅ Identify the three to five most important results that must be achieved before December 31.
✅ Ensure that every critical commitment has a responsible executive and a measurable outcome.
The final two months can significantly influence an organization’s annual results, stakeholder confidence, and readiness for the next financial year.
When the CEO establishes clear priorities and reinforces accountability, the organization is better positioned to finish the year with discipline and purpose.
Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.
